# A program's method named like a builtin's is the program's: a component's
# `replace` and a struct's `upper` are called as written, not spelled as the
# string methods of the same name.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Name {
    first string
}

func Name.upper(n Name) => "<{n.first}>"

component box ui.node {
    var (
        xs list[int] = [1, 2]
        n = Name{first="ada"}
    )

    func replace() {
        xs = [7]
    }

    ui.text #out(value="{xs.length()} {n.upper()}")
    ui.button #b(text="go", @click { replace() })
}

func testComponentMethod(t Test, c box) {
    c.replace()
    t.assert(c.out.value == "1 <ada>")
}

func testFromAHandler(t Test, c box) {
    c.b.click()
    t.assert(c.out.value == "1 <ada>")
}

ui.window {
    box
}
-- testrun/html/none/app.sngl/box/1 --
